column1: cad26b|Score by throwing Bean Bags into Goals; the higher the goal, the more points. A robot can carry only one bean bag at a time, and most bean bags have to be fetched from across the whole field.
7d83fb|Bean Bag
9a86a2|The only scoring object. Red, blue and yellow, 38 in all: 16 red, 16 blue, 6 yellow (2 of them are Preloads brought onto the field at the start, one per team).
c597b1|Floor Goal
40d19d|One each for red and blue, the floor area from next to the pyramid's L1 to the edge of the field.
c9b10e|Pyramid Goal
0d0c2b|One each for red and blue, with three levels: L1, L2 and L3.
b2ba18|The gray top surface of one tower; it has no color.
fbe933|Load Zone
9620c6|One each for red and blue, in the corners. People at the field edge put bean bags in one by one (only the matching color).
93fc9e|Teamwork
52b9a5|Two teams per alliance, one robot each, scoring together within 1 minute. **There is no autonomous period**; it's driver-controlled throughout.
aae4c1|Driving Skills
10672c|One team, one robot, 1 minute of driving by hand.
2e7d2a|Autonomous Coding Skills
c85482|One team, one robot, 1 minute **running only on its own program**, with no controller. This is the event where you most need to practice coding!
7ceebe|The skills ranking is the sum of the "driving" and "autonomous" scores. Skills scoring rules are the same as Teamwork.
8f2131|L4 Goal (yellow only)
9fb9a1|A bean bag must be "the same color as the goal" or "yellow" to score in floor goals and L1–L3.
e008e0|The L4 goal takes only yellow bean bags.
dfe6e5|If one bean bag counts at several levels, only the highest level's points count.
b52cc0|Scoring happens after the match ends and everything has stopped, judged visually by the referee.
c8339f|Size
f41f01|At pre-match inspection and at the start of each match, the robot must fit within 11" × 20" × 15" (about 279 × 508 × 381 mm).
8ad9e7|At most 6 VEX IQ Smart Motors. Extras count too, even if not connected.
0c39ca|Brain and Controller
127e21|One Brain and one Controller per robot; no other microcontrollers (such as Raspberry Pi or Arduino).
5ff6cd|Parts
220c8c|Only official VEX IQ parts may be used (except the listed exceptions); 3D-printed parts aren't allowed.
a8e9ff|Inspection
a479d3|The robot must pass inspection before every match.
ed6293|Hands out of the field
a8311a|During a match, team members can't touch the field, the robot or the bean bags (except with a referee's permission).
f89351|Don't start early, don't be late
72c611|Move only after the timer starts, and the robot must stop when time is up.
77ef88|Handle only one bean bag at a time

529bda|A robot may "hold" at most one bean bag at a time, or push one bean bag along the floor (Plowing, manual SG6). Carrying or pushing several at once is a violation. See the original manual for details.
882342|Safety first
7441f3|Unsafe operation can get a team disqualified. Students must be accompanied by an adult, and every team member needs a signed participation consent form.

e4bec2|Only one bean bag at a time → the value of each "run" varies a lot: a Floor throw is 1 point, L3 is 12, L4 is 16. Higher levels score more but the mechanism is harder to build. First work out: how many seconds per run? At most how many runs in 60 seconds?
a7cc1b|There are only 6 yellow bean bags, L4 (16 points) takes only yellow, and yellow can also go in a goal of any color → yellow is precious, so plan how to get it.
e37187|Teamwork has two robots → you can divide the work (one fast on low levels, one on high levels), and agree on routes so you don't block each other.

5c2559|The 60-second autonomous skills run has no driving → the route must be fixed and run the same every time. Reliability beats flashiness: get "one scoring action" working every time, then add more.
4c575f|The two skills scores are added → driving practice builds mechanisms and operating skill, autonomous practice builds accuracy; practice both.
27ee9e|Motors
9431b8|There are 2 on the field. A gray horizontal surface on top of a tower, with no colour.

9b967c|Two teams form an alliance, one robot each, and score as much as they can in 1 minute. There is no autonomous period; it is all driver control, and the two drivers swap controllers halfway through the match (at about 30 seconds).
b62782|One team, one robot, 1 minute that runs on its own code only, with no controller. This is the event where you most need to practise your programming!
68c224|A bean bag must not touch any robot to score (the same for the Floor Goal, L1–L3 and L4).
226d8a|Floor Goal: the bean bag must be "entirely" inside the goal; if even a small part sticks out past the boundary it does not score.
c42a85|L1–L3 and L4: the bean bag must touch that level's surface, or sit on a bean bag that touches the surface; an L1–L3 bean bag also must not touch anything outside the field.
142696|A bean bag touching a robot does not score

a7a5af|Scores are checked after the match ends and everything has come to rest. If a bean bag is still touching a robot (for example the arm is still pressing on it), that bean bag does not score, so after the last trip move the robot off the bean bag (after time runs out the robot may not move any more). (Manual SC3–SC5)
